title: Andrew W. Lo, MIT 15.401 Finance Theory I — Lectures 18–20: Capital Budgeting (2007–2008)
use: NPV choice, incremental after-tax cash and working capital, project interactions, IRR limitations and risk/date matching.
verification: Actual official 37-page PDF text inspected: slides 3–10, 18, 20–31 and 34–35. Some equation glyphs are absent from extracted text; chapter formulas and original numerical cases were independently derived and checked rather than attributed to unseen glyphs. Dated market beta examples and historical survey statistics are not reused. No copied exercises or universal current-tax claim.

title: Aswath Damodaran — Applied Corporate Finance, Chapter 6: Project Interactions, Side Costs, and Side Benefits
use: Feasible project combinations, explicit replacement assumptions for unequal lives, owned-resource opportunity costs and baseline-dependent cannibalization.
verification: Actual author-hosted 45-page PDF inspected in scoped sections: capital-rationing setup and limitations, PDF pages 1–5; equivalent-annuity/replication and generalized horizon comparison, PDF pages 11–13; opportunity costs and cannibalization, PDF pages 14–17. The text's broad IRR-reinvestment narrative and heuristic project-ranking claims are not adopted: this chapter derives comparisons algebraically and enumerates its finite constrained set. Old company examples, forecasts and tax facts are not used as current evidence. Original chapter examples do not reproduce the source cases.

title: OpenStax Principles of Finance — 16.2 Net Present Value (NPV) Method
use: Dated cash-flow timeline, present-value subtraction and a basic NPV profile as a complementary introductory route.
verification: Actual section body inspected, including definition, equation and the source timeline/table; no source figures or exercises reproduced. The chapter supplies its own opportunity-rate, funding and mutual-exclusion conditions. Linked IRR section was inspected for context but is not cited or adopted as authority for a mechanical reinvestment assumption.
